transcript.statement: Sustainability is crucial for the autonomous driving system, as it directly impacts energy efficiency and the carbon footprint. GRN-01 ensures energy consumption is minimized, while GRN-02 promotes renewable energy use. GRN-03 focuses on lifecycle assessments to reduce resource impact. GRN-04 enhances energy recovery during braking, and GRN-05 targets emission reductions. GRN-06 optimizes routing for energy efficiency, and GRN-07 establishes protocols to minimize energy usage during failures. These requirements align with global sustainability goals and enhance the system's public acceptance.

transcript.statement: Performance efficiency is vital for the autonomous driving system to ensure quick and responsive operations. EFF-01 aims for a 30% reduction in travel time, enhancing user experience. EFF-02 maintains jerk below 0.5 m/s³ for comfort, while EFF-03 ensures safety during Minimal Risk Maneuvers. EFF-04 focuses on real-time ODD compliance monitoring, and EFF-05 targets a 95% success rate in speed profile generation. EFF-06 emphasizes quick processing for obstacle constraints, and EFF-07 prioritizes smoothness during emergencies. However, I see conflicts with GRN-01, as reducing travel time may increase energy consumption, and SAF-04, which may limit performance during critical maneuvers.

transcript.statement: Trustworthiness is essential for the autonomous driving system to protect user data and ensure system integrity. TRU-01 mandates end-to-end encryption for user data, safeguarding privacy. TRU-02 enforces role-based access control, limiting permissions to enhance security. TRU-03 ensures auditability by logging access and modifications to critical data. TRU-04 incorporates data anonymization techniques to protect identities. TRU-05 requires regular security audits to identify vulnerabilities. TRU-06 ensures secure remote updates to maintain system integrity. TRU-07 informs users about data collection, fostering transparency and trust. These requirements are crucial for user confidence and regulatory compliance.

requirements.text: The system shall implement a multi-layer safety architecture including passive, active, and functional safety mechanisms to ensure collision protection and fail-safe operations.
The system shall execute a Minimal Risk Maneuver within 5 seconds upon detecting critical system failures while allowing a controlled increase in jerk to prioritize safety.
The system shall continuously monitor Operational Design Domain compliance and issue a human takeover request when boundaries are approached.
The system shall maintain jerk below 0.5 m/s³ during normal operation while allowing a controlled increase during Minimal Risk Maneuvers.
The system shall satisfy curvature constraints ($kappa$) to prevent rollover during maneuvers at all speeds.
The system shall utilize iterative quadratic programming to handle non-convex obstacle constraints reliably within a response time of 100 milliseconds.
The system shall optimize path planning to achieve a minimum 30% reduction in average travel time while minimizing energy consumption.
The system shall implement end-to-end data encryption for all user data transmitted to protect privacy and ensure data integrity.
The system shall enforce role-based access control to restrict user permissions based on their role within the system.
The system shall log all access and modifications to critical data for auditability purposes.
The system shall conduct regular security audits at least bi-annually to identify and mitigate potential vulnerabilities without interfering with real-time operations.
The system shall ensure compliance with the Apollo Pilot Safety Report and EM Motion Planner specifications at all operational times.
The system shall document all safety and compliance-related decisions and changes for accountability and regulatory purposes.
